evidence.paraphrase: Sages ask who previously gained merit by hearing the text. Suta introduces a speech-impaired sage and Lomasa, who visits Brahmaloka, bows, sits as permitted and asks Brahma to recite the Ganesa Purana previously told to Vyasa. Brahma agrees.

Beings are disturbed; gods and sages petition Sankara, who comes with Parvati, attendants and petitioners and sees his emaciated, anthill-covered body.

boons_and_powers.motive: Conquer the cosmic egg through austerity (1.23.40).
boons_and_powers.austerity_or_circumstances: Five-syllable formula received from Sukra; secluded forest, no food for1000 divine years, mantra repetition, meditation on Sadasiva and Pasupata initiation. Gods and sages petition Siva because of the disturbance (1.23.41–49).
boons_and_powers.requested: Fearlessness everywhere; devotion to Sadasiva; no death from anything composed of five elements and three gunas; lasting lordship with health; sovereignty over the cosmic egg (1.24.24–26).
boons_and_powers.granted: Siva grants all that was requested, explicitly attributing the grant to the fierce austerity (1.24.29).
boons_and_powers.mechanism: Death protection is formulated by the composition of its possible source: all that has the five elements and three gunas (1.24.25); no narrower countermechanism read.
boons_and_powers.restrictions: The death-protection request names the five-element/three-guna domain. No further exceptions examined.
boons_and_powers.duration: The requested lordship is called lasting; the death-protection request says never. All requests are granted; there is no separate temporal expiry clause in the read passage.
boons_and_powers.notes: Trigger unstated in extracted grant. Counter and eventual defeat unexamined; null is not evidence that there is no counter. Compound requested benefits kept in one source speech record.

narrative_events.details: The sages ask Suta for a past example of the merit produced by hearing the Purana. He introduces a sage who could not speak.
Lomasa reaches Brahmaloka, bows to Brahma and sits with permission. He requests the Ganesa Purana that Brahma had narrated to Vyasa; Brahma invites him to listen carefully.
Brahma tells the Purana to Lomasa. The speech-impaired sage listens devotedly to the complete recitation. He subsequently speaks fluently, studies and recites the text for others.
narrative_events.outcome: The listener gains speech and becomes a reciter.

narrative_events.cause: The text presents this as the result of devotional hearing.
narrative_events.details: The sage enjoys desired pleasures and gains sons and grandsons. At life’s end he reaches Ganesa’s auspicious abode.
narrative_events.outcome: The bounded example reaches its final outcome.

narrative_events.details: The narrator describes Saṃvaraṇa as an Ikṣvāku-line king devoted to sacrifice, giving, study and protecting his subjects. Childless, he performs a putriya sacrifice complete with its prescribed elements, gifts and food distribution. He then hears Harivamsa and rewards the reader and Brahmins; neither brings a son.

narrative_events.cause: The sage proficient in Ganesa Purana arrives at the king’s house.
narrative_events.details: Saṃvaraṇa asks the sage to stay, joyfully hears the Purana from him and rewards him with jewels, pearls, garments and golden ornaments. The king gains a son, becomes devoted to Ganesa, enjoys many pleasures and finally attains Ganesa’s highest state.

narrative_events.cause: His sister hears that her brother gained offspring by hearing the Purana.
narrative_events.details: The king’s unnamed sister summons the same sage and listens to the Purana. She gains a brave son, becomes devoted to Ganesa, has sons and grandsons and enjoys pleasures. At life’s end she reaches Ganesa’s own abode.
narrative_events.outcome: The sister’s hearing episode reaches its final outcome.

narrative_events.cause: Indra’s attraction during the festival and encounter with Durvasas.
narrative_events.details: After Rambha’s festival performance, Indra goes into a forest with her. Seeing Durvasas, he leaves her and bows; his seed falls on the ground. Matsara arises from that seed. Earth nurtures him, names him Matsara and arranges initiation at five. He studies and marries Madakara, daughter of Durbuddhi.

narrative_events.cause: Matsara decides to conquer the cosmic egg by intense austerity.
narrative_events.details: Matsara obtains the five-syllable formula from Sukra and propitiates Sambhu. He stays in a secluded forest, observes Pasupata initiation, fasts for a thousand divine years, repeats the formula and meditates on Sadasiva. His austerity disturbs gods and beings. Gods and sages seek Sankara’s protection; Sankara comes with Parvati and his attendants. They see Matsara reduced to skin and bones, covered by an anthill.

narrative_events.cause: Siva is pleased with Matsara’s austerity.
narrative_events.details: Siva awakens Matsara and invites his wishes. Matsara regains strength on seeing him, bows, worships and offers a hymn. After Siva renews the offer, Matsara asks for universal fearlessness, devotion, immunity from death caused by the five-element and three-guna domain, health with lasting lordship, and sovereignty over the cosmic egg. Although the request astonishes the assembly, Siva grants all of it because of the fierce austerity.
narrative_events.outcome: The requested compound boon is granted.

narrative_events.details: Matsara returns home, making friends, his mother and wife glad, and enjoys pleasures. Madakara bears him two sons: the elder Sundarapriya and younger Visayapriya.

narrative_events.cause: Demons gathered at his father-in-law’s house seek conquest with his boon-supported strength.
narrative_events.details: The assembled demons urge Matsara to conquer the gods. He says that he wants this too, but Earth restrains him because Indra is his father and gods deserve honor. The demons counter with their own account of Jalandhara, argue that gods are enemies of demons, and tell Matsara to leave Earth. He accepts this advice, which the narrator calls harmful, abandons Earth and stays with them.
narrative_events.outcome: Matsara transfers allegiance; subsequent army and conquest episodes remain unexamined.

story_spines.title: The speech-impaired sage hears Brahma’s recitation and gains speech
story_spines.completeness_basis: The question introducing the example, narration request, hearing, transformation, subsequent recitation, descendants and final abode are all read and extracted; verse33 explicitly introduces another ancient account.
story_spines.editorial_notes: Completeness is limited to this nine-verse narrative, not chapter155 or wholeGanesa Purana. Muka is not conflated with any independently named sage.

story_spines.title: Saṃvaraṇa and his sister obtain offspring after hearing Gaṇeśa Purāṇa

story_spines.editorial_notes: Source presents devotional efficacy, not a literal individually spoken boon. Do not convert these results into an explicit divine boon grant.
